mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a fall in housing starts (HOUST) below 700K signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 400,000 in a single month, accompanied by a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.4 percentage points, signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 400000 AND UNRATE falls > 0.4pp in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a recovery in aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a month-over-month increase in INDPRO of more than 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns within the short horizon.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO MoM change > 0.5% and positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns falls below 0.3 or is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample testing.
